messages:
olivia-meridian: Hey team — after we flipped on autoscale-snapshots yesterday, we started seeing user-facing 429s. Happens in bursts every few minutes for ~10–20s. Not a cron. Example request id: req_9f3b. Anyone seen something like this?

emma: Thanks for the report. Can you paste one raw response (headers + body) and tell us whether you share the same API key across pods/services? Also which endpoint — embeddings / chat / completions?

olivia-meridian: Embeddings endpoint (/v1/embeddings). We do share the same API key across a few worker fleets. Sample response we captured: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
x-rw-rpm: 320
x-rw-tpm: 5400
x-rw-rpm-limit: 500
x-rw-tpm-limit: 3000
x-rw-retry-after: 8
x-request-id: req_9f3b
{ "error": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED", "message": "tpm limit hit" }
```

We also noticed our client-side retries do immediate exponential backoff starting at 100ms, but many workers start at same time when they process S3 events.

emma: Got it. Two things jump out: 1) x-rw-tpm (5400) > x-rw-tpm-limit (3000) — you're hitting the per-minute token limit, not RPM. 2) shared API key across fleets plus synchronous retries + S3 fanout can create a short-term concurrency spike (high TPM) even if avg RPM is fine.

raj: tagging infra-bot to check recent ingress patterns for that key. infra-bot: can you post minute-by-minute ingress counts for req key?

infra-bot: Found spike for api_key=key-meridian-01 — 1842001200..1842001260 window:
```
minute 1842001200 tokens: 4800 requests: 900
minute 1842001260 tokens: 10200 requests: 1700
```
Spike aligns with S3 event fanout (multiple lambda-like workers).

tilly: Quick diagnostic suggestions:
- Confirm whether your HTTP client is using HTTP/1.1 (new TCP/TLS per request) vs HTTP/2 multiplexing. Many small parallel requests with short-lived connections inflate TPM due to TLS handshakes and our per-request token accounting.
- Check whether the SDK option keepalive:true is enabled to reuse connections.
- Add jittered stagger to worker start (random 0-3s) and increase initial backoff to 500ms.

olivia-meridian: We're on an internal SDK wrapping fetch. I just checked — keepalive was false. We also launch up to 200 parallel workers on snapshots. That probably matters.

emma: Recommended immediate mitigations (quick to deploy):
1) Turn on HTTP/2 or enable keepalive / connection pooling in your SDK. That alone reduces per-request overhead.
2) Add a lightweight client-side concurrency cap (p-limit 20) while you smooth the workload.
3) Increase initial retry backoff to 500ms + add jitter. Respect x-rw-retry-after when present.
4) If this is business-critical and sustained, consider Redwood Dedicated or a temporary TPM quota bump — we can fast-track for a few hours.

olivia-meridian: Will try 1–3 now. Can you open a short-term quota bump while we test? Our workers are user-impacting.

emma: I filed a support escalation to infra (linking raj). ETA for temporary quota increase: ~30–45m pending quick review. Please keep us posted on impact after enabling keepalive and concurrency cap.

raj: I pushed a short window increase: api_key=key-meridian-01 tpm_limit bumped from 3000 -> 6000 for 1 hour; noted in infra queue (INC-18420). Monitor for further abuse.

olivia-meridian: After enabling keepalive + cap=20 + jitter, the 429s dropped to almost zero in our first test run. Thanks! We'll keep monitoring.

tilly: Follow-up items before we close:
- olivia: share SDK code snippet for connection creation so devex can recommend best config.
- emma: confirm that the temporary quota bump will be removed automatically after 1 hour.
- raj: evaluate whether this customer's access pattern should move to Dedicated or receive a permanent quota increase if this workload is regular.

emma: Confirmed — temporary bump auto-expires. We'll review telemetry and suggest next steps in 24h. :thumbsup:

olivia-meridian: Sending SDK snippet and a short replay trace in #support-attachments. Very relieved, thanks everyone!

infra-bot: Note: We also observed a small cluster of requests from an older SDK version that did parallel retries without honoring x-rw-retry-after. If you still see 429s after changes, pls flag and we'll trace those client IDs.

emma: Great—closing this thread once we have the SDK snippet and 24h telemetry. If anyone else hits similar pattern, share these mitigations: enable keepalive/HTTP2, client concurrency cap, respect retry-after, consider Dedicated for large background fanouts.
